title.narrative: ILO, 2022-2025, Decent Work and Labour Rights in Southern Africa
ILO, 2022-2025, Decent Work and Labour Rights in Southern Africa

description.narrative: Det aktuella projektet har arbetande fattiga unga, män och kvinnor som målgrupp. Det bygger på ett starkt partnerskap mellan International Labour Organisation (ILO), Southern African Development Community (SADC) och dess medlemsländer, och viktiga intressenter såsom The Southern African Trade Union Coordination Council (SATUCC) och SADC Private Sector Forum (SPSF). Projektet kommer att arbeta på två nivåer med syftet att stärka SADC-sekretariatets kapacitet att förespråka uppskalning av systeminsatser; föreslå och främja effektiva policyförändringar i dess medlemsländer samt att driva på långsiktiga och hållbara förbättringar för utsatta unga, kvinnor och män i byggnadssektorn (sub-regional nivå). Dessutom kommer nationella projekt att genomföras liksom samarbete med nationella regeringar, privata aktörer, fackföreningar och arbetsgivarorganisationer i Moçambique, Zimbabwe och Sydafrika för att ta itu med viktiga systembegränsningar i en sektor där den stora majoriteten arbetskraft är lågavlönad och där bristande säkerhet och informell anställning är rådande. De tre föreslagna länderna har identifierats och valts ut på grund av deras snabbt växande byggnadssektorer, underskott i anständiga arbetsvillkor liksom på grund av existerande erfarenheter och relationer med nyckelpartners och pågående relaterade utvecklingsinsatser.

Targeting the working poor young, men and women, and the micro, small and medium sized enterprises (MSMEs) of the building construction sector that employ a majority of the labour force in the Southern Africa sub-region, the Project builds on an already strong partnership between International Labour Organisation (ILO), Southern African Development Community (SADC) and its member states, and vital stakeholders such as Southern African Trade Union Coordination Council (SATUCC) and SADC Private Sector Forum (SPSF). Adopting a market systems development approach, the Project will work on two levels aimed to strengthen the capacity of the SADC Secretariat to advocate for scaling-up systemic interventions; propose and promote effective policy change across its member states, and drive long-term and sustainable improvements for vulnerable female and male labourers in the building-construction sector (sub-regional level); and to implement national projects and engage with national governments, private sector actors, trade unions and employers organisations in Mozambique, Zimbabwe and South Africa by addressing key systemic constraints in the sector in which the vast majority of workers are locked in low wage, inadequate safety and informal employment (see footnote). The three suggested countries have been identified and selected due to their growing construction sectors, decent work deficits as well as experiences and relationships with key partners and ongoing related interventions.

The project objective is to contribute to improved labour rights in the building-construction sector in the Southern Africa Development Community. The project, which will be implemented using a systemic approach to decent work and will work at the sub-regional level (Outcome 1) as well as in three countries: South Africa, Mozambique and Zimbabwe (Outcome 2).
The project will aim to improve labour rights through targeting interventions that provide benefit to the working poor and young women and men and the micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) that employ them. These target groups include the workers who are most likely to have few labour rights - including poor wages, occupational safety and health, contract stability and informality and the MSMEs, who disproportionately struggle to provide decent work to their employees relative to larger contractors.
As the project will be grounded in a systemic approach to decent work, it will strive to benefit the target groups in long-term sustainable way that can reach scale. It will do this by working through key project partners, including the South African Development Community (SADC), regional and national employers associations and trade unions, SADC member government bodies and the private sector.

The project team has laid the groundwork in the three countries and has after some delay now transitioned to the implementation phase, under which numerous activities are underway. The Embassy notes that the time needed to secure country level partnerships was significantly more time consuming than initially anticipated.
ILO's partnership with SADC is at last fully in place and the SADC Secretariat is actively involved in the project. In addition to this accomplishment, the following are examples of key activities and achievements to date: Market systems analyses (MSA) in the three countries were completed and the project's Theory of Change was subsequently revised to reflect the MSA outcomes. Pilot intervention models for promoting decent work and productivity were then designed, based on the findings of the MSAs. The learnings from Outcome 1 will be shared with SADC to promote scale beyond the three target countries. Country level working groups have been established in all three countries. The working groups have identified social protection, labour inspections, contracting, freedom of association and representation as the most relevant focus areas for the implementation phase. An unexpected issue was identified which has led to plans to produce a comparative study on maternity protection. The study will include recommendations and best practice with the aim to inform policy making in the SADC region.
Progress was made in the collaboration with the trade unions and with Business Development Service providers in the three countries, and more concrete outcomes from these developments are expected by the end of the year
